rationale: Roberts is most likely to keep the opinion to a narrow RJR Nabisco step-two “focus on domestic use in commerce” rule and to manage the Court’s effort to cabin Steele v. Bulova without adopting an effects test. Sotomayor is likely to write a lone dissent advocating a cabined substantial-U.S.-effects approach, while a few majority justices may add short concurrences to emphasize textualism (Thomas/Gorsuch) or comity/administrability limits (Alito/Barrett).
